ball.bounce_anchor_uncertainty.notes: The anisotropic sigma and the ray-frame residual weighting are wired and default-on. They are a CORRECTNESS fix to a mis-stated uncertainty, not an accuracy improvement: the ball is no more accurate than before, we have stopped overstating how accurate it is, and the reported sigma is now LARGER. What is PENDING is apply_bias_correction, which would MOVE the anchor and is therefore off by default; the systematic away-from-camera overshoot is reported for consumers to act on, never silently applied. The bias magnitude depends on a per-sport bounce vertical-speed prior, and the defaults here are pickleball priors that have NOT been measured against pickleball ground truth. External validation is table tennis only. VERIFIED=0 for pickleball.

ball.ray_court_volume_gate.notes: REFUTED, and kept only so the refutation stays executable. Background-ball acquisition itself is CONFIRMED: on the frozen 167-row judge all 11 indoor hidden false positives are real pickleballs that are not the ball in play, and on burlington the detector tracks the adjacent court for tens of consecutive frames. This gate does not catch it. Measured across 1269 emitted detections on the four owner clips with reviewed metric_15pt calibrations, the ray-misses-the-volume rate is 0.0/1.3/0.0/0.0 percent at margin 2 m and apex 8 m, and the only settings that flag anything also suppress owner-clicked real-ball pixels (2 of 17 on outdoor_webcam_20s at margin 0.5 m). The cause is geometry: a camera behind the baseline sees an adjacent court through its own airspace, so on burlington frame 30 a ball 19 m outside our sideline has a ray that crosses our near-baseline corner about a metre up, and at the 2 m margin the burlington camera centre itself lies inside the volume, making the test vacuous on that clip. It is also unscoreable on the frozen judge, whose two sources both carry calibration_grade=failed with a null frozen_calibration. Never promote on the strength of this entry; it is a necessary condition only and buys no precision. VERIFIED=0.

ball.subframe_bounce_timing.notes: Default OFF. The bounce-anchor overshoot is caused by anchoring at the wrong INSTANT, not by a noisy pixel: contact falls between frames, the marked frame still shows the ball above the plane, and forcing that ray to z=ball_radius overshoots along the ray by height/|ray_z| -- a quantity that is never negative, hence a bias. This entry finds the instant instead of widening the error bar around the wrong one. World position is continuous through a bounce and world velocity is not, so the 2D track has a kink at exactly the contact instant; fitting the incoming and outgoing image branches with a shared meeting point yields the instant and the sub-frame pixel from one fit, with no calibration input. On TT3D the median 3D bounce error falls 0.0911 -> 0.0306 m and the systematic along-ray bias falls +0.0993 -> -0.0076 m over the same 816 bounces. The downstream weak-segment 3D metric did NOT follow: median improved 19.8% while p90/p95/max regressed, inside a metric with comparable run-to-run spread. PENDING because (a) that is TABLE TENNIS -- 25 fps, a 40 mm ball with 3.3x the drag; the timing GEOMETRY transfers exactly but the magnitudes do not, and (b) it MOVES the anchor and its time, so it changes solver output and must not switch on without pickleball ground truth. On the owner's 7 wolverine bounce labels the estimator fires on 4 (median shift 0.19 m, |dt| 0.13-0.36 frames) and abstains on 3; those labels are ray-plane intersections at a marked frame themselves, so they carry the same overshoot and are NOT independent ground truth. The timing sigma is floored at 0.25 frame intervals because propagating pixel noise alone was measured 5.4x optimistic against TT3D. The reported bias term shrinks by the timing error removed and no more: it still reads +0.055..+0.092 m on TT3D against a measured residual of -0.008..-0.014 m, i.e. deliberately conservative. apply_bias_correction remains OFF and separately PENDING under ball.bounce_anchor_uncertainty. VERIFIED=0 for pickleball.

proven_against.card: TT3D external validation: 816 scored bounces (136 x 3 views x 2 noise conditions)
proven_against.downstream_weak_segment_3d: MEASURED NEGATIVE: median 0.1336 -> 0.1071 m but p90 0.792 -> 0.914, p95 1.403 -> 1.713, max 4.75 -> 5.09, and fitted trajectories 498 -> 473. E2 is nondeterministic run to run by a comparable margin, so the direction is unsettled; either way the downstream reconstruction is NOT demonstrated to improve.
